name: Traditional Chinese
modelReview: artifacts only, 2026-11-19, by Claude Fable 5.2: a rule book (answers.md) derived from usage notes written in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan first, Hong Kong and Macau marked) by a writer told nothing of cron; a lexicon; and hand-written rows for the visible and held-out grids, hard cases and options. No renderer exists yet. The rows pass the oracle checks (coverage, no pattern twice, equal schedules worded alike); the author worked out the firing times of each row and re-read it once. Nothing has been read by a blind reader, no native speaker of Taiwan or Hong Kong has seen any of it, and the open-web searches for corpus evidence found almost nothing exact, so the taste calls rest on the usage notes and the author's own judgment. Later on 2026-11-19 a blind judge briefed only in Chinese read 110 sentences and an adversarial read worked all 624 rows against their patterns: two wrong schedules, four second readings and several usages a Taiwan editor would not write were found; the rule book was amended first and every affected row rewritten by hand (the 每次在 family replaced by 每N小時的…, 每天 after a range of dates, the date as base where both day fields must match, months and years listed with 的, 次月, 雙數年, single times after their rate). None of the changed forms has been read since. The Hong Kong style in particular (12-hour 時 times, 星期, 中午12時 and 凌晨12時 in place of the notes' 正午 and 午夜) is unreviewed.
